neighbours.label: Modifier naming an acquired chromosomal or genetic lesion in diseased cells (chromosomal, genomic, somatic, translocations in tumour and marrow findings); inherited-family talk stays quiet
fire: Marrow cytology in this lymphoma case uncovered chromosomal deletions affecting the short arm.
Pathologists reviewing the glioma slides noted genomic instability across many tumour clones.
Biopsy of the melanoma showed somatic changes that were absent from healthy skin.
Karyotyping of the myeloma cells detected balanced translocations between two chromosomes.
Screening of the embryos identified chromosomal errors that had arisen after fertilisation.
Cancer cells in that cohort accumulate genetic abnormalities as the disease progresses.
Her oncologist ordered a panel to look for structural rearrangements within the tumour.
Analysis of the blasts revealed molecular aberrations linked to a poor prognosis.
quiet: Marrow donation in this lymphoma case required a matched sibling from the same household.
Pathologists reviewing the glioma slides noted swelling across many nearby blood vessels.
Biopsy of the melanoma showed a clear margin that was wide enough for healthy healing.
The condition runs through three generations of the family and passes from mother to son.
Screening of the newborns identified hearing loss that had gone unnoticed after delivery.
